text:
🚨To our dear friends in the free democracies of the world,

I am a young Korean. 

Since December 3, 2024, liberal democracy in the Republic of Korea has vanished. 

Our country is rapidly becoming a vassal of the Chinese Communist Party and the North Korean regime. Lee Jae-myung, a fake president installed through a fraudulent election in which the Chinese Communist Party intervened, is handing the whole of the Republic of Korea over to them. 

President Yoon Suk-yeol and First Lady Kim Keon-hee, who truly loved this country and stood with the free democracies, are enduring this very hour in solitary cells too small to turn around in.

We Koreans are resisting this regime fiercely, every single day, with everything we have, including our lives. 

But for some thirty years the Chinese Communist Party has been swallowing Korea slowly, according to a larger plan. It planted spies across politics, the economy, defense, culture, education, and diplomacy, and passed laws little by little, eating the country out from within.

Because democracy in Korea is gone, writing a letter like this can send me to prison, and it can put my life in danger. Even so, to protect the homeland I love, I am writing this with everything I have.

Koreans learned only yesterday that the Lee Jae-myung government had been sending fuel to Russia. We learned it later than you did. In the Korean press, the story was not heard at all. Many people heard it for the first time only when you began to speak of it. It shows how deeply the Korean media has fallen under the influence of the Chinese Communist Party.

On October 6, 2026, the Guardian, citing port records and ship-tracking data, reported that in July and August more than 176,000 tons of fuel, most of it diesel, was loaded in Korea for Russia. Seven tankers made fourteen voyages to the Russian Far East. Three of those ships are under British and European Union sanctions. Some listed Japan or Singapore as their destination before heading to Vladivostok, and one took on cargo through a ship-to-ship transfer off the Korean coast. In August, Russia imported 368,000 tons of oil products by sea, the highest monthly figure since the full-scale invasion. Of that, 112,000 tons, about 31 percent, came from Korea. That month Korea was Russia’s second-largest supplier, after India.

Caught, and far from apologizing, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea issued a statement saying it was not true. And today, October 8, the ministry announced that it had decided to recall the ambassador to Ukraine. Six days after Lee Jae-myung said on October 2 that if Ukraine continued to refuse to acknowledge the facts and offer a public apology over the repatriation of North Korean prisoners, further measures would follow, he decided to bring Ambassador Park Ki-chang home.

Koreans truly did not know about the fuel shipments to Russia. For Lee Jae-myung, however, this is no surprise.

Why?

In 2019, while he was governor of Gyeonggi Province, he was accused of having the Ssangbangwool Group deliver 8 million dollars to North Korea on his orders. The indictment said 5 million dollars went to a smart-farm project in South Hwanghae Province and 3 million dollars to preparations for a planned visit to the North. In a related case, the court found that about 3.94 million dollars of that 8 million had been sent illegally, including 2 million dollars paid to the Workers’ Party of Korea as visit expenses. The sentence of former vice governor Lee Hwa-young, seven years and eight months, is already final. Lee Jae-myung’s own trial is still in the first instance.

He did not want to go to prison, and the presidency let him postpone that trial. So in June 2025 he made a deal with the Chinese Communist Party and became president through a fraudulent election. After taking office, he began to deliver what he had promised China: the whole of the Republic of Korea. If the Party is to cross the Pacific and invade the American mainland, it must first take Korea, which lies on that path. He is not a president lawfully chosen by the Korean people. That is why we are not demanding impeachment. We are demanding that the election be voided. He has never once been the president of our country.

Once in power, he abolished the prosecution service that had existed in Korea for 78 years and replaced it with a new Public Prosecution Office. It was not only the name that changed. The prosecution Koreans knew is gone. Since October, signs have been coming down across the country, and even the word “prosecution” engraved on manhole covers is being ground off. Six and a half billion won of our taxes has already been allocated just to erase that name. That covers only the cost of stripping logos and lettering from the walls, glass, and signs of 67 institutions. Identification cards, business cards, computer systems, and subway signs cost still more. All of it is for one man. A Korean who becomes the victim of a crime can no longer properly expect the protection of the law.

That old remittance to the North was not the end. His government budgeted 1.023 trillion won for the Inter-Korean Cooperation Fund in 2026. But according to Export-Import Bank of Korea data released by People Power Party lawmaker Kim Sang-hoon, the execution rate from January through July was only 1.1 percent. The money actually spent through July was about 11 billion won. As of October, about 990 billion won remains. We cannot help asking why money that is not even being used is set aside every year, and where the rest is meant to go. As always, the purpose of this money is clear. It is money for the dictatorship next door that is trying to bring South Korea down.

Today most Korean ministers are under the control of people tied to the Chinese Communist Party. Official statements issued in the name of the Korean government are that party’s voice. That is why they condemn Ukraine so harshly. Democratic Party lawmakers represent those interests so completely that one could mistake them for Chinese. 

The current Minister of Unification, Chung Dong-young, an agent of the Chinese Communist Party, publicly mocked a lawmaker of North Korean defector background in the National Assembly just yesterday, after that lawmaker raised the forced repatriation of defectors. He is also the one who announced that 166 kinds of medical equipment, 1,431 items in all, would be sent to a hospital in Kangdong County, Pyongyang. That is 6.75 million dollars, about 9.3 billion won. Some of it, including ambulances and CT scanners, is subject to United Nations sanctions, but exemptions have already been granted. The plan is to bring it into Nampo port as early as next month. Whether it remains medical equipment, or is converted into missiles, no one can know.

The Ministry of Employment and Labor is the same. Seventy percent of Korea’s unemployment benefits go to Chinese nationals. National health insurance is the same. So many Chinese recipients have drawn from it that the system is in deficit, and it has recently come out that people who had already returned to China kept receiving Korean government subsidies for a long time. Gyeonggi Province, in the capital region, is in effect bankrupt. After Lee Jae-myung served as governor, two Democratic Party governors spent the budget so freely that no one can say where it went. The most likely places are North Korea or China. 

Because of this, support for pregnant women and newborns for the rest of 2026 has simply disappeared. The national support of 500,000 won a month per newborn was cut on the grounds of fiscal difficulty, while 150 billion won is set aside for infants in the North. Will that money really reach the children, or will it come back as missiles that kill our soldiers? As always, it comes back as the second.

Dear friends, we do not know where our money is going.

From July 7, 2026, the Lee Jae-myung government amended the Information and Communications Network Act. A Korean who criticizes Lee Jae-myung and his government can now truly go to prison. Freedom of the press in Korea is gone. Young Korean soldiers are dying under suspicious circumstances inside their units, one by one, day after day, for no reason anyone can explain, and a young patriotic leader died overnight. North Korea does not cross in secret. In broad daylight it crosses the border and plants mines for ten hours a day. Our government does nothing. 

On September 21, 2026, three soldiers of the 25th Division were wounded by one of those mines while clearing a patrol route in the western Demilitarized Zone. One lost a hand, another a leg. It was about ten meters south of the Military Demarcation Line. 

Do you know what the Korean Ministry of National Defense, occupied by spies, said about this? 

“Is there evidence that it was a North Korean mine? Could it not have been a South Korean mine? What if speculation like that spreads and plants prejudice against North Korea?” 

Friends, is this the Ministry of National Defense of South Korea, or of North Korea? Lee Jae-myung has not said a single proper word toward the North. Compensation for these young soldiers is pitiful. Even if a battalion commander who lost his foot is recognized as wounded in action, the lump sum is about 89.25 million won, roughly $66,000, and the monthly allowance is 90,000 won, about $67. Why? Because under Lee Jae-myung, Korean money must be sent to North Korea and China.

Koreans learned only recently, from the news, that our soldiers had been standing guard toward the North without live ammunition. They keep the border with empty rifles. The ministry told young soldiers to stand guard without bullets, with batons alone. Put simply, it told them to die in front of the North Korean army.

Recently a Chinese agent was caught giving orders on Instagram. His profile listed the plan to communize Korea like this :

• Dismantle the prosecution (completed) 
• Dismantle the judiciary (in progress) 
• Dismantle the conservative party (2027) 
• Dismantle the Ministry of National Defense (2028) 
• Dismantle Samsung, Hyundai, SK, Hanwha, LG through candlelight protests (2029) 
• Policy orders: implement a communist system (called “basic income”), expand foreign voting rights.

When that account was exposed, he posted this: 

“So what can you Koreans even do? 
Just open your eyes and watch your country become communist.”

In Korea, one of the strongest Christian nations in Asia, freedom of religion is now disappearing as well.

Right now, Lee Jae-myung and the Democratic Party of Korea, backed by the Chinese Communist Party, are putting unprecedented pressure on the church. Since February 2026, legislation has been proposed that would impose heavy taxes on overseas mission funds. South Korea sends more missionaries than any nation in the world except the United States. They are trying to stop that. 

There is also discussion of a law that would dissolve religious corporations if churches speak about politics. The assets of any dissolved church would go entirely to the state. Many pastors who raised their voices against the communization of this country have already been imprisoned. In plain language: 

even as a Christian, either remain silent about communism, or lose everything.

There is still one piece of good news. On September 30, 2026, President Trump and the United States Secretary of Commerce announced that Korea would invest more than 50 billion dollars in the Alaska LNG project. Lee Jae-myung will not have expected that announcement. Putting that money into the United States is, for him, a danger from his masters in the Chinese Communist Party. So the Korean government rushed to say that the Alaska investment was not confirmed, that it depended on commercial viability, and that it would not exceed the agreed ceiling of 200 billion dollars in total and 20 billion dollars a year. I sincerely hope Korea keeps the promise it made to the United States and does not delay it.

Because of this investment, it has become harder for Lee Jae-myung to spend as he pleases the Inter-Korean Cooperation Fund he has piled up for the North, the roughly 990 billion won still unused. That is why his government keeps attacking Ukraine and stirring up trouble. The North was supposed to receive the money and did not, and so it is angry. When you see a Korean politician attacking Ukraine, read it as tears squeezed out by fear of China and the North, and as flattery meant to look good in Beijing and Pyongyang.

Dear friends in the free democracies of the world, Koreans are resisting the Lee Jae-myung regime with everything we have. If you watch our protest videos, the photographs of Korea today, and the posts I put up, you will feel how hard we are fighting for a change of regime. From babies to the elderly who can barely walk, every generation is out in the streets without a single day’s rest, shouting, 

“Lee Jae-myung’s election is void!"

“Chinese Communist Party, get out of Korea!”

"Destroy communism!”

Young Koreans rush into the streets every day to protest, shout until their throats give out, and wake the nation. They film what they see and spread the news of resistance on social media. 

But a young person has had every bank account frozen simply for criticizing the government. Koreans in their twenties are being taken to prison for protesting for liberal democracy. Patriots have died in freezing cells. People who could not bear the grief have set themselves on fire to condemn the government. Someone died, crushed beneath a police bus, while trying to stop President Yoon Suk-yeol from being taken to prison. Countless elders, after years of trying to stop communization, were beaten to death.

Even so, we will not stop until we take back a free and democratic Republic of Korea.

Lee Jae-myung’s end is slow, but it is coming in a way that cannot be turned back.

The Korean people have woken up. Lee Jae-myung’s approval is now at the bottom. Men and women, old and young, want to see him fall. Lee Jae-myung is anxious. He is begging North Korea, China, and Russia to save him. But his end is already written. 

The proof is that you are reading this letter. Until now, censorship kept this truth from reaching the world. Now it is coming out.

Even if Korea appears to have turned its back on Ukraine and the free democracies of the world, dear friends, remember how the true president of our country, Yoon Suk-yeol, treated you.

He promised real support to Ukraine, and he delivered a substantial part of it. He could not deliver all of it. The Democratic Party, which took a parliamentary majority through a fraudulent election in which China intervened, cut his government’s 2025 budget to zero. The president’s operating expenses, support for the young, support for newborns and the elderly, industrial investment: all of it became zero won. Even the budget for the president’s overseas trips was cut in full. The support President Yoon had promised Ukraine was also cut to zero by the Democratic Party.

Because of that budget disaster, and because of the countless crimes of the National Election Commission seized by the Chinese Communist Party and of the Democratic Party, the security of the Republic of Korea was collapsing. That is why, on December 3, 2024, President Yoon Suk-yeol declared martial law. But the Democratic Party put an “insurrection” frame on President Yoon and First Lady Kim Keon-hee, as if they were a threat to the state, and locked them in prison. The two of them are now suffering in a room of 3.3 square meters, less than one pyeong.

I am a young Korean. 
Many people tell me I have a long life ahead of me.

But I would rather choose death than watch the Republic of Korea become a communist country.

We know the true face of communism better than anyone. 

We see that face in our countrymen in the North, who have been without freedom for 78 years. 

If we give up, the other half of our people will lose their chance at freedom forever. 

That is why we cannot give up. 
The Republic of Korea will defend its liberal democracy.

And one day, we will bring home the other half of our nation from a country where a person can be shot for owning a Bible, and where an eight-year-old was executed for licking sugar scattered on a state-owned sugarcane field because he was hungry. We will reunify our country in freedom and democracy, together with our people who still suffer in silence in North Korea.

And we will repay the debt of gratitude we owe to the twenty-two free democracies that, in 1950, willingly staked their lives to save the Republic of Korea from communism. The young people of those countries gave their lives in the Korean War for Koreans like me. We will never allow their deaths to become a wasted page of history.

Every citizen of the Republic of Korea has staked their life. That is why we are not afraid.

“Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather, be afraid of the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.” 
— Matthew 10:28

I sincerely hope the Republic of Korea recovers its true president and its national dignity, and that its bond with the free democracies of the world grows firmer still. Even in this hard time, I pray for peace upon you, your families, and your countries. I can pray this only because I believe in God.

It was our God who, in 1948, when Korea was founded and every other leader said communism was good, established a liberal democracy through our founding president, Syngman Rhee, the one man who loved Him.

I believe in the God who, in 1950, when the communist army had occupied all but one corner of the Republic of Korea, saved our country through the Incheon landing of General MacArthur, a man who loved Him.

South Korea has already survived crisis after crisis of communization. 

This time, too, we will win. 

Because more than seven thousand in the Republic of Korea have not bowed the knee to Baal. 

And because our God is always good.

#YOON_AGAIN

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. Bhai aur beheno, agar aap bhi Binance P2P trading karte ho aur suddenly bank account freeze ho gaya hai toh pareshan mat ho. Yeh bahut common problem hai India mein. Innocent log bhi fas jaate hain jab kisi buyer/seller ka paisa kisi fraud case se link hota hai.

Yeh steps follow karo - 

1️⃣ Sabse Pehle Bank Branch Jaao  
   - Freeze ka exact reason, Cyber Crime complaint number, IO naam aur Police Station details lo.  
   - Written notice maang lo.

2️⃣ Saare Proofs Collect Karo (Bahut Important)  
   - Binance P2P complete order history (screenshots)  
   - Buyer/Seller ke saath chat  
   - Payment proof (UPI, bank transfer screenshot)  
   - Bank statement jisme transaction dikhe  
   - Aadhaar, PAN, Binance account details

3️⃣ Binance Support ko turant contact karo  
   - App mein Help section → Submit ticket  
   - Order ID aur proofs attach karo. Woh counterparty ko investigate kar sakte hain.

4️⃣ Cyber Cell mein Representation Daalo  
   - Local Cyber Police Station ya online portal pe jaao.  
   - Detailed application likho ki transaction genuine tha Binance P2P pe hua.  
   - Saare proofs attach karo.  
   - Lawyer (Cyber crime specialist) ki madad le lo - yeh bahut kaam aata hai.

5️⃣ Follow-up karte raho  
   - Har 7-10 din mein bank aur cyber cell ko call/email karo.  
   - Partial release ke liye request kar sakte ho.

• P2P ke liye alag dedicated bank account use karo (savings account mat use karo)
• Sirf verified buyers/sellers ke saath trade karo

• Binance P2P risky hai India mein, agar ho sake toh avoid karo

Statement: Instagram censors a cartoon about censorship. IFF will challenge it.
A cartoon on comedy, copyright and the IT Rules has been withheld in India by an automated system that cites no order and gives no reasons.

On 27 October 2026, Instagram withheld in India a cartoon by Aadvik (@aaaaadvik ) who first published on 29 September 2026 as a collaborative post on the accounts of IFF, Aadvik and stand-up comedian Pulkit Mani. It shows a panicked man at a console in the image and style of the Prime Minister with red buttons marked "Censor", "Copyright" and "IT Rules", while a comic performs on a screen above him. Its caption reads, "Quick, check if comedy counts as a violation of copyright or a matter of national security." The post asked who decides what gets taken down, and on what grounds.

Instagram has now answered this literally by taking it down after close to a month. Its notice says access was restricted "through an automated system implemented pursuant to legal requirements" under the IT Rules, 2021. It names no order, authority, provision or ground. There was no prior notice and no chance to respond. The same cartoon remains available on IFF's X account. The post also carried an update on Pulkit Mani v. Meta Platforms Inc. & Ors., his Delhi High Court suit over fraudulent copyright strikes on his Instagram page, in which IFF appears for him pro bono. Meta, a defendant in that suit, has now hidden a post about it from Indian users in which it is the principal defendant.

In 1945, George Orwell wrote a preface to Animal Farm, a book four publishers had turned down. He noted, "the sinister fact about literary censorship in England," he observed, "is that it is largely voluntary." Unpopular ideas, he argued, could be silenced without any official ban, by institutions that guess what power wants and act first. The preface itself stayed unpublished until 1972 and in Nineteen Eighty-Four he gave this habit a machine, namely, the memory hole, a slot at the Ministry of Truth into which inconvenient records vanished, unexplained and beyond appeal. Today, the Ministry of Electronics and IT acts as this Ministry of Truth that covers up its gross incompetence in securing our cyber security by building an architecture of digital censorship that is implemented by technology platforms. It is under these IT Rules, 2021 that Instagram's "automated system" exists as a memory hole. It has swallowed a cartoon whose whole joke is a man reaching for the censor button without asking what comedy is. The absurdity Aadvik drew has now been actually demonstrated in stark reality.

This machine did not build itself and in April 2026, The Hindu reported that Meta automatically restricts content flagged by government and police in India, and wants a fresh government direction before restoring anything later found lawful. MeitY's unpublished advisories of 8 and 10 October 2026 pressed platforms, and Meta by name, for "enhanced diligence". The same notice has been served on cartoonist Satish Acharya, who lost nine cartoons and then his account, on journalists covering the October protests, and days ago on comedian Kajol Srinivasan. The Union Government applies the pressure and Meta has chosen to answer it with a system that censors first and explains nothing.

IFF will soon challenge Meta's automated restriction system in an appropriate legal proceeding. A joke is not a threat to the nation, and we will not let Meta’s algorithms decide otherwise.

Our demands
1) Meta must restore the post in India, and tell IFF, Aadvik and Pulkit Mani which order, authority and provision it relied on, if any.
2) Meta must suspend the automated restriction of content in India and disclose the inputs on which its "automated system" acts.
3) MeitY must state whether any direction, Sahyog Portal intimation or advisory concerned this cartoon, and withdraw and publish its advisories of 8 and 10 October 2026.
4) The Union Government must restrict content only by reasoned, published orders under Section 69A or by intimations that comply with Rule 3(1)(d), and never by leaning on platforms.

Speak up
A memory hole works only as long as people accept it in silence. If you are a cartoonist, comic, creator or journalist whose post or account has been withheld with this notice, write to us at legal@internetfreedom.in with screenshots of every notice and we will try our best to provide you help pro-bono. Over the past 72 hours we have assisted close to 56 social media users, some of whom had their accounts restored. We are in this together!

text:
IFF statement on the geo-blocking of 26 Reddit posts in India

On 21 October 2026, Reddit, Inc filed with the Lumen Database a government takedown order from India covering 26 URLs and complied, so that all 26 posts are now geo-blocked in India (Lumen notice 100411498). The notice names neither a law nor an agency, since its “Laws/Regulations” field is blank and the request is attributed only to an “Agency”. The 26 posts sit in 18 subreddits, from r/Northeastindia to r/IndianDefense and r/myanmar, and were catalogued on 24 October by @geoblockedindia in a thread that also carries images of the notice.

Irrational censorship does not advance national interest

Nearly all of the blocked posts concern the India–China border. They include open-source verification of PLA footage from the June 2020 Galwan clash, satellite imagery reported by Indian newsrooms, a Caravan essay, a TRT World report on Beijing’s claim over Arunachal Pradesh, maps ranging from the one China draws to users’ sketches of proposed new states, and a question put to Chinese users. Several are five or six years old, and three had already been deleted by their authors.

IFF condemns this order as secret, disproportionate and unlawful. We do not dispute that the State may act against speech that genuinely endangers the defence of India, such as troop positions, operational plans, the identities of serving personnel or a hostile state’s coordinated information operation, and the twenty soldiers who died at Galwan deserve a country that takes its border seriously. Nothing on this list is of that kind, because every item was already public, whether released by the PLA, reported by Indian newsrooms or posted by ordinary users. Post 14 describes Indian soldiers holding off an armoured vehicle with sticks, stones and helmets, and their courage is not a secret, nor is there any reason to make it one.

Arunachal Pradesh is part of India and the country asserts that position with confidence, so it has no need to hide from its own citizens the map that Beijing draws, which they need to know in order to answer. Censoring Indian's discussion of the dispute does nothing to weaken China’s position and hands Chinese state media a ready story about Indian censorship. Two of the blocked posts, numbers 11 and 13, were themselves objecting to wrong maps, while others are users’ sketches of proposed new states. The secrecy surrounding the order protects no one but the official who signed it.

Whether this was a direction under Section 69A and the Blocking Rules, 2009, or a notice under Section 79(3)(b) routed through the Sahyog portal, it fails the tests the Supreme Court has set. Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) 5 SCC 1 upheld Section 69A only because the 2009 Rules require written reasons, a hearing under Rule 8 and review under Rule 14, and none of these safeguards was observed here. A restriction must also be necessary and the least restrictive means available, and this order is neither, since blocking six-year-old threads answers no present danger, blocking posts already deleted shows that nobody examined the list, and blocking entire threads silences commenters nobody considered.

How Reddit works

Reddit is a federation of tens of thousands of communities known as subreddits, each created by users and run by unpaid volunteer moderators, while Reddit, Inc itself handles legal demands. Reddit says that content named in a government request is checked first against its own rules and then against local and international law, including human rights standards, before access is restricted in the requesting country, after which a reader in India sees a restriction notice while everyone else, including anyone in India using a VPN, still sees the post (Reddit Transparency Report, July–December 2025).

Because each post sits at a fixed URL with a threaded discussion beneath it, a block by URL hides the whole thread, including every reply beneath it, and r/Northeastindia has lost seven threads about its own borders for readers in India while a reader in Shanghai can still open them. The moderators who built these forums receive no notice and have no appeal, and the only public record of the order is the notice Reddit chose to send to Lumen.

Takedowns on Reddit are rising

India is now the second-largest source of the government takedown demands that Reddit receives. Between July and December 2025, Reddit received 169 such requests from 28 countries, of which India sent 21, second only to the UAE (Reddit Transparency Report, July–December 2025), up from fewer than ten in all of 2019. The demands have also grown bolder, as a 2025 order relayed through Pune Police named 825 posts about a matrimonial service and warned of a countrywide ban if Reddit did not comply, yet Reddit refused and the court agreed with it. Across all platforms, published analysis puts MeitY’s blocking orders at about 12,600 in 2024 and 24,300 in 2025. On 21 October 2026, Reddit complied with all 26 URLs without any public challenge.

Our demands

1. MeitY and the originating agency must publish the order, the provision invoked and the reasons for each URL.

2. The order must be withdrawn and access restored, and any post said to be unlawful must first go through notice and a hearing under Rule 8.

3. The Review Committee under Rule 14 must examine the order and publish its finding.

4. If the order came through the Sahyog portal, the Government must say so and stop using Section 79(3)(b) against speech while the courts decide its legality.

5. MeitY must disclose how many Reddit URLs it has had blocked since 2024, and on what grounds.
